descripcion: At A2 you build the first conditional for a real, possible future situation: if it rains, we'll stay home. The if-clause always uses the present simple, never will. These forms are the building blocks for more nuanced modal use at higher levels.

filas: We'll stay home if it rains.

ejemplos.texto: If it rains, we'll stay home.
If you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus.
I'll call you if I have time.

notas: The if-clause uses the present simple, even though it's about the future.
Will never appears inside the if-clause.
The order of the two parts can be switched.

contraste.es: El español usa si + presente y futuro simple, con lógica idéntica al inglés. El error típico es poner will también en la cláusula con if.

errores: Forgetting the comma when the if-clause comes first.

traducciones.de: Wenn ich sie sehe, werde ich…
Wenn es sonnig ist, werden wir…

autochequeo: Is the if-clause in the present simple?
Is there no will in the if-clause?
Have I built at least two conditional sentences?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the first conditional. Check for will inside the if-clause and check the comma. Do not rewrite the text. Flag anything unclear. Check whether the sentence sounds natural, not translated from Spanish.
